lafayette: Emma Lou had been to the Lafayette before with John and had been shocked by the scantily clad women and obscene skits.
They made their way to the Lafayette, the Jew’s gift of entertainment to Harlem colored folk.
Then followed the usual rigamarole carried on weekly at the Lafayette concerning the undesirability of black girls.
About three-quarters of the people at the Lafayette tonight were either dark brown or black, and here you are crying and fuming like a ninny over some reference made on the stage to a black person.
Alva was to take Emma Lou to the midnight show at the Lafayette Theater.

The midnight show at the Lafayette on Friday is quite a social event among certain classes of Harlem folk, and, if one is a sweetback or a man about town, one must be seen standing in front of the theater, if not inside.
